_comment: Evaluable hold-detector configurations. Apache-2.0 model families only
Ultralytics code and weights are AGPL-3.0 and are forbidden in this repo.
RF-DETR input resolutions must be divisible by patch_size * num_windows (32 for the nano/small/medium detectors, 12 for seg-nano).

num_classes=1 rebuilds the detection head for the single `hold` class instead of carrying RF-DETR's 90-class COCO head into the export, which buys no file size (class-dimension tensors are negligible) but drops 89 dead logits per inference.

nano-tiled-1024.notes: The phone candidate. Smallest Apache-2.0 RF-DETR, four tiles per photo.

nano-tiled-1024-classical-mask.notes: Same weights as nano-tiled-1024, plus a classical in-box segmentation so the renderer gets an outline instead of a ring. Outlines are cosmetic, so this config exists to measure what a box-only detector costs at mask IoU.

nano-untiled-1024.notes: The phone candidate without tiles: the spike showed 2x2 tiling hurts on the ~800 px Roboflow photos (each tile loses the wall context and upscales the holds), so this config gives the same nano weights one full-frame pass instead. Model input is 768, not 1024: the DINOv2 backbone's attention is quadratic in tokens, and 1024-px training (which rfdetr's multi-scale aug pushes to 1184) ran ~70x slower per step than medium-untiled on MPS. 768 is still 2x the tiled config's per-pass resolution and the source photos are ~800 px on the long side.

small-tiled-1024.notes: Middle rung. Same tiling as nano so the two are comparable.

medium-untiled-1280.notes: The quality ceiling the phone configs are judged against. One pass over the whole photo.

seg-nano-tiled-1024.notes: Real instance masks from the model. Heavier to train and to export; kept so the classical-mask config has something to be compared with.
